title: Stable Plant Structure Reconstruction via Geometry-Regularized 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Plant 3D reconstruction from multi-view images is essential for image-based phenotyping, but thin and self-occluded organs remain difficult to reconstruct reliably. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables efficient reconstruction, its photometric optimization does not explicitly constrain Gaussian morphology, allowing primitives to over-expand in weakly observed regions or stretch excessively along thin leaves and stems. We propose a geometry-regularized 3DGS framework that treats Gaussian morphological stability as both an optimization objective and an evaluation target. The method combines scale-ratio regularization to suppress extreme anisotropy and absolute-scale regularization to limit oversized primitives, without organ-specific structural assumptions. We further introduce primitive-level metrics, including 95th-percentile primitive scale, maximum-axis scale, axis ratio, and floating-artifact rate, to assess stability beyond PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. Experiments on tomato, soybean, and maize show that the method preserves rendering efficiency while reducing Gaussian morphological degeneration.
